LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard AUR PKGBUILD for packaging an upstream AppImage release of OpenWhispr. The source is fetched directly from the project's own GitHub releases page (`https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/download/...`), which is the expected upstream. A proper SHA-256 checksum is provided and pinned, so the binary integrity is checked at build time.

The `prepare()` function chmods the downloaded AppImage executable and then invokes `--appimage-extract` to unpack the squashfs contents into `$srcdir/squashfs-root/` without executing the application itself. The `package()` function performs routine packaging: installs the AppImage to `/opt/openwhispr-appimage/`, creates a thin shell wrapper at `/usr/bin/openwhispr` that re-execs the AppImage, patches the embedded `.desktop` file's `Exec=` line to use the wrapper, installs icons from the hicolor tree, and installs the license file. There are no suspicious network requests, no obfuscated or encoded payloads, no `eval`/`base64` usage, no `curl|bash` patterns, and no operations outside the expected package scope.

The wrapper script simply `exec`s the installed AppImage — standard practice for AppImage packaging. All optdepends (`ydotool`, `xclip`, `xsel`, `wl-clipboard`, `xdotool`, `wtype`, etc.) are listed as optional runtime helpers, which is normal for a dictation/clipboard tool. Nothing here suggests a supply-chain attack.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard AppImage PKGBUILD with pinned source and checksum; no malicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>
